title: Design Sprint Strategy: Speeding up product development with world-class planning processes
image1Description: Learning the Design Sprint process to plan and test Startup products systematically

section1.heading: Origin and Intent
section1.content: In Startup development, a common problem is taking too much time to plan and not starting the work. I joined the Design Sprint training to learn a Framework that helps shorten work time from many months to just a few days. My intent was to create a clear Roadmap of what should be done first or later, and at what time to bring the MVP for testing for the best efficiency. This ensures that every resource used accurately meets the business model.

section2.heading: Role and Action
section2.content: I practiced project management through 5 important steps of Design Sprint: Understanding the problem (Understand), creating options (Diverge), deciding on the best solution (Decide), building a prototype (Prototype), and testing with real users (Validate). My role was to connect business needs and technical possibilities to set the priority (Prioritization) of developing various features to match the Startup timeline.

section3.heading: Challenges
section3.content: The main challenge was balancing 'Speed' and 'Accuracy' (Speed vs. Accuracy). Deciding on important features under time limits and planning work to meet customer needs as close to 100% as possible required careful analytical thinking. I had to learn how to cut out unnecessary things so the Product is sharp enough to truly function as a Startup Product.

section4.heading: Results and Learning
section4.content: This training gave me a work mindset that focuses on being 'Fast but careful' (Agile Mindset). I can plan work with a clear structure, knowing when to develop and when to test ideas. This experience helped me become a team leader who can run projects in the right direction, reduce confusion in the team, and increase the chance of success in delivering products to the market systematically.
